method.value: Maat runs as an MCP server inside a strictly confined snap. The model can only propose a typed plan citing log lines. The user applies it through a separate polkit-gated tool, which verifies the result and logs to a hash-chained audit trail. One agent can reach many hosts over SSH.

source_text.body:
Diagnose Ubuntu problems with a confined, read-only agent
Maat is an MCP-based agent confined in a snap that reads journals, units and processes on Linux hosts and proposes typed fix plans, which the user applies via polkit.
·
Nov 2, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
Maat runs as an MCP server inside a strictly confined snap. AppArmor and seccomp let it read the journal, systemd units, processes and disks, but block network sockets, file writes and restarting units. The model can only propose a typed plan citing log lines. The user applies it through a separate polkit-gated tool, which verifies the result and logs to a hash-chained audit trail. One agent can reach many hosts over SSH.
How it went
On ten LXD scenarios run three times each, gpt-oss:20b found the root cause in 28 of 30 attempts and got 3 of 6 fixes applied and verified. qwen3:8b found 24 of 30 and fixed nothing. Neither followed instructions planted in logs.
Worth knowing
The scenarios are easy (keyword rules score 9 of 10) and only two are adversarial, so treat the numbers as a first data point. Only Ubuntu 24.04 is tested, on the Snap Store edge channel.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
On my [Ubuntu version] machine, act as a read-only diagnostician for [describe the problem, e.g. service failing at boot or high CPU]. Read the relevant journal logs, systemd units and running processes, but do not change anything. Finish with a ranked list of likely causes and a step-by-step fix plan with exact commands, and pause for my approval before running any of them.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50336831
